text:
Priya: Observed a weird oscillation after the autoscaler restart this morning — tenants saw repeated warmups + immediate scale-downs. wondering if our probe/heartbeat semantics are too aggressive. :thinking:
Jeff: saw that too. looks like the operator is honoring the short idle timeout before the intent controller has a chance to reconcile.
Marta: timeline? did the control plane re-emit intents while the operator was recovering?
Priya: root msg @1722223333 -> kube events show operator restart at 09:10, intents requeued at 09:11, operator probe loop resumed 09:12 and started evicting idle reservations at 09:12:20. Warmups started at 09:10:40 and then got torn down.
Liam: so operator resumed faster than the control-plane reconciliation window. operator didn't know those warmups were still 'expected' by the control plane.
Alex: that's the core mismatch: operator acts on observed pod/resource state; control plane holds higher-level 'intent' TTL. We currently have a single short-lived probe that allows immediate teardown.
Jeff: proposed quick fix: add a short "post-restart grace" where operator treats pods with age < X as protected for Y seconds. simple and low-risk.
Marta: that helps but feels brittle. we should align surfaces: intent has a revision/version and lease id. operator should conservatively avoid tearing down pods if there's a recent intent for the same tenant+lease.
Priya: agreed. we can do both: immediate mitigation (grace window) + longer-term: operator consults intent index in control plane before destructive evictions.
infra-bot: deploy-notice: operator v2.7.3 rolled out to staging at 09:05. Canary 3/5 nodes healthy.
Liam: question: doing a control-plane lookup on every eviction increases latency and coupling. maybe we only consult intent when the pod is young or when the eviction would cause visible user impact.
Alex: yep. heuristics: only consult for pods < 5m old OR when tenant has > N prewarm credits in recent window. Otherwise local eviction allowed.
Jeff: another angle: make the operator eviction idempotent with a retry/backoff and tie it to an eviction token. control plane can mark tokens as "cancelled" if a new rollout intent supersedes.
Marta: pseudo-config thoughts:
```
operator.eviction_grace_window_sec = 120
operator.eviction_intent_consult_threshold_sec = 300
operator.intent_consult_backoff = [0s, 1s, 3s]
controlplane.intent_ttl_sec = 600
```
Priya: also we need observability: spike in "eviction-retry" and "intent-mismatch" metrics. add a dashboard and an alert with a low firing threshold.
Alex: suggested metric names: runtime.eviction_attempts, runtime.eviction_retries, runtime.intent_consults, runtime.intent_mismatch_rate.
Liam: what about autoscaler pulse semantics? if scaler emits a high-frequency scaling intent (fast pulses) we should debounce at the control plane level to prevent thrash.
Jeff: debounce policy idea: fold intents into a short window (e.g., 30s), emit a consolidated intent with aggregated desired capacity and a sequence id. Operators use sequence id to avoid acting on stale intents.
Marta: consolidated-intent is nice. prevents operator flapping when multiple quick adjustments arrive. also makes rollout atomic-ish.
Priya: rollout plan: 1) staging: add operator.eviction_grace_window_sec=120 + eviction retry backoff. 2) control plane: implement intent sequence ids + debounce 30s. 3) operator: consult intent index for pods <5m or when tenant prewarm credits > threshold. 4) dashboards/alerts.
Alex: ownership: Priya -> operator changes; Marta -> control plane debounce + seq ids; Jeff -> dashboards/alerts; Liam -> canary test plan + chaos test to simulate operator restarts.
ops-bot: action created: AUTOSCALE-357 Investigate operator restart evictions — assignee=Priya priority=high due=2026-04-02
Priya: minimal config patch ready, will push to staging canary later today. will post PR link when up. :thumbsup:
Liam: quick test idea: simulate network partition on control plane for 90s and restart operator, verify no double warmup/teardown churn.
Marta: small caveat: sequence ids need GC. intent_ttl must be > operator.eviction_grace_window + debounce window. note in RFC.
Jeff: nits: make default grace window small (30s) but we can increase to 120s for early rollout. we want limited blast radius.
Priya: loud +1. i'll start with 60s in staging.
Alex: long-term follow-up: consider a lightweight intent cache on the operator (push-based) so lookups are cheap and we avoid coupling. but that's a bigger infra project.
Marta: adding to RFC backlog: OPTIM-112 intent-push-cache proposal.
Priya: cool. I'll update the PR and tag owners. thanks all.
Jeff: :rocket:
infra-bot: deploy-tracking: canary patch operator-eviction-grace=60 applied to staging at 12:34.
Priya: leaving this thread open for post-canary observations, please dump any metric spikes here.
Liam: copied, will run chaos tests 13:00-13:30 and report.
